context.body: John sees a new heaven and new earth, God dwelling with people, death and pain passing away, and the declaration, “I am making all things new.”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The Bible’s closing vision uses creation language to describe a changed world and renewed divine-human dwelling.
observations.label: New heaven and new earth: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Death and pain absent visible within its account or reuse of creation.
observations.label: New heaven and new earth: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: God dwells with people · New heaven · new earth · city · Former things pass → all things new · Death and pain absent · First creation · new creation
observations.label: Relationships named in Revelation 21:1–5

payload.posture: Read Revelation 21:1–5 as its own new creation creation setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places First creation · new creation inside this creation setting without making it a conclusion for every creation passage.
